D&D5e.AbilityStr: Strength measures bodily power, athletic training, and the extent to which you can exert raw physical force.
D&D5e.AbilityCon: Constitution measures health, stamina, and vital force.
D&D5e.AbilityInt: Intelligence measures mental acuity, accuracy of recall, and the ability to reason.
D&D5e.AbilityWis: Wisdom reflects how attuned you are to the world around you and represents perceptiveness and intuition.
D&D5e.AbilityCha: Charisma measures your ability to interact effectively with others. It includes such factors as confidence and eloquence.
D&D5e.SkillAcr: Your Dexterity (Acrobatics) check covers your attempt to stay on your feet in a tricky situation, such as when you're trying to run across a sheet of ice, balance on a tightrope, or stay upright on a rocking ship's deck.
D&D5e.SkillAni: When there is any question whether you can calm down a domesticated animal, keep a mount from getting spooked, or intuit an animal's intentions, the GM might call for a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check.
D&D5e.SkillArc: Your Intelligence (Arcana) check measures your ability to recall lore about spells, magic items, eldritch symbols, magical traditions, the planes of existence, and the inhabitants of those planes.
D&D5e.SkillAth: Your Strength (Athletics) check covers difficult situations you encounter while climbing, jumping, or swimming.
D&D5e.SkillDec: Your Charisma (Deception) check determines whether you can convincingly hide the truth, either verbally or through your actions.
D&D5e.SkillHis: Your Intelligence (History) check measures your ability to recall lore about historical events, legendary people, ancient kingdoms, past disputes, recent wars, and lost civilizations.
D&D5e.SkillIns: Your Wisdom (Insight) check decides whether you can determine the true intentions of a creature, such as when searching out a lie or predicting someone's next move.
D&D5e.SkillItm: When you attempt to influence someone through overt threats, hostile actions, and physical violence, the GM might ask you to make a Charisma (Intimidation) check.
D&D5e.SkillInv: When you look around for clues and make deductions based on those clues, you make an Intelligence (Investigation) check.
D&D5e.SkillMed: A Wisdom (Medicine) check lets you try to stabilize a dying companion or diagnose an illness.
D&D5e.SkillNat: Your Intelligence (Nature) check measures your ability to recall lore about terrain, plants and animals, the weather, and natural cycles.
D&D5e.SkillPrc: Your Wisdom (Perception) check lets you spot, hear, or otherwise detect the presence of something. It measures your general awareness of your surroundings and the keenness of your senses.
D&D5e.SkillPrf: Your Charisma (Performance) check determines how well you can delight an audience with music, dance, acting, storytelling, or some other form of entertainment.
D&D5e.SkillPer: When you attempt to influence someone or a group of people with tact, social graces, or good nature, the GM might ask you to make a Charisma (Persuasion) check.
D&D5e.SkillRel: Your Intelligence (Religion) check measures your ability to recall lore about deities, rites and prayers, religious hierarchies, holy symbols, and the practices of secret cults.
D&D5e.SkillSlt: Whenever you attempt an act of legerdemain or manual trickery, such as planting something on someone else or concealing an object on your person, make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check.
D&D5e.SkillSte: Make a Dexterity (Stealth) check when you attempt to conceal yourself from enemies, slink past guards, slip away without being noticed, or sneak up on someone without being seen or heard.
D&D5e.SkillSur: The GM might ask you to make a Wisdom (Survival) check to follow tracks, hunt wild game, guide your group through frozen wastelands, identify signs that owlbears live nearby, predict the weather, or avoid quicksand and other natural hazards.
D&D5e.SchoolAbj: Abjuration spells are protective in nature, though some of them have aggressive uses.
D&D5e.SchoolCon: Conjuration spells involve the transportation of objects and creatures from one location to another.
D&D5e.SchoolDiv: Divination spells reveal information, whether in the form of secrets long forgotten, glimpses of the future, the locations of hidden things, the truth behind illusions, or visions of distant people or places.
D&D5e.SchoolEnc: Enchantment spells affect the minds of others, influencing or controlling their behavior.
D&D5e.SchoolEvo: Evocation spells manipulate magical energy to produce a desired effect.
D&D5e.SchoolIll: Illusion spells deceive the senses or minds of others.
D&D5e.SchoolNec: Necromancy spells manipulate the energies of life and death.
D&D5e.SchoolTrs: Transmutation spells change the properties of a creature, object, or environment.

D&D2024.AbilityStr:
Strength measures physical might.

Strength Checks

Make a Strength check to lift, push, pull, or break something.

Saving Throw

Make a Strength saving throw to physically resist direct force.
D&D2024.AbilityDex:
Dexterity measures agility, reflexes, and balance.

Dexterity Checks

Make a Dexterity check to move nimbly, quickly, or quietly.
D&D2024.AbilityCon:
Constitution measures health and stamina.

Constitution Checks

Make a Constitution check to push your body beyond normal limits.
D&D2024.AbilityInt:
Intelligence measures reasoning and memory.

Intelligence Checks

Make an Intelligence check to reason or remember.
D&D2024.AbilityWis:
Wisdom measures perceptiveness and mental fortitude.

Wisdom Checks

Make a Wisdom check to notice things in the environment or in creatures' behavior.
D&D2024.AbilityCha:
Charisma measures confidence, poise, and charm.

Charisma Checks

Make a Charisma check to influence, entertain, or deceive.
D&D2024.SkillAcr: Examples: Stay on your feet in a tricky situation, or perform an acrobatic stunt.
D&D2024.SkillAni: Examples: Calm or train an animal, or get an animal to behave in a certain way.
D&D2024.SkillArc: Examples: Recall lore about spells, magic items, and the planes of existence.
D&D2024.SkillAth: Examples: Jump farther than normal, stay afloat in rough water, or break something.
D&D2024.SkillDec: Examples: Tell a convincing lie, or wear a disguise convincingly.
D&D2024.SkillHis: Examples: Recall lore about historical events, people, nations, and cultures.
D&D2024.SkillIns: Examples: Discern a person's mood and intentions.
D&D2024.SkillItm: Examples: Awe or threaten someone into doing what you want.
D&D2024.SkillInv: Examples: Find obscure information in books, or deduce how something works.
D&D2024.SkillMed: Examples: Diagnose an illness, or determine what killed the recently slain.
D&D2024.SkillNat: Examples: Recall lore about terrain, plants, animals, and weather.
D&D2024.SkillPrc: Examples: Using a combination of senses, notice something that's easy to miss.
D&D2024.SkillPrf: Examples: Act, tell a story, perform music, or dance.
D&D2024.SkillPer: Examples: Honestly and graciously convince someone of something.
D&D2024.SkillRel: Examples: Recall lore about gods, religious rituals, and holy symbols.
D&D2024.SkillSlt: Examples: Pick a pocket, conceal a handheld object, or perform legerdemain.
D&D2024.SkillSte: Examples: Escape notice by moving quietly and hiding behind things.
D&D2024.SkillSur: Examples: Follow tracks, forage, find a trail, or avoid natural hazards.
D&D2024.SchoolAbj: Abjuration spells prevent or reverse harmful effects.
D&D2024.SchoolEvo: Evocation spells channel energy to create effects that are often destructive.
D&D2024.SchoolIll: Illusion spells deceive the mind or senses.
